full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J : This rule by plaintiff of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 filed for specific performance of contract, against principal defendants-appellant of Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009, directed against judgment and order dated 25-4-2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur allowing Miscellaneous Case No. 455 of 2008 filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure thereby set-aside the judgment and decree dated 29-4-2008 subject matter of Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009. 

 2. The aforesaid suit was suit was filed by the plaintiff petitioner against defendant No. 1, Mst. Rana Noor, for specific performance of contract in which Government of Bangladesh was made proforma-defendant. The suit was decreed. Rana Noor defendant No. 1, having aggrieved filed the Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009 which is pending before this Court. While decree was passed on 29-4-2008, as Government of Bangladesh was made proforma defendant, did not appear filed Miscellaneous Case No. 455 of 2008 on 20-10-2008 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Appeal was tendered on 7-1-2009. Defendant No. 1 also obtained an order of stay of the execution proceedings on 20-10-2009. 

 3. In the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is stated that Government having been made proforma defendant did not take proper attention to the summons which was served on the Government, as such, government did not take proper care and step in the proceeding of the suit. It is specific case of the Government that, 

 4. In this Miscellaneous Case, plaintiff appeared and filed written objection. There-after, disappeared. Learned Joint District Judge while allowing the Miscellaneous Case found inter alia that, since defendant Government was not made principal defendant but proforma defendant, Government did not take proper step in the proceeding of the suit. The finding of the learned Joint District Judge is that :— 

 "Defendants could not take proper steps in the suit. The suit properties are government properties. The Plaintiff-opposite-parties proclaimed in the area that he had got decree in the suit regarding the Government properties. The defendants inquired about the matter and according to the information slip they got information that the suit was decreed on contest on 29-4-2008. The PW 1 gives deposition supporting the above claim of the partition. The information slips (Exhibit-2) so that the defendants-opposite parties came to know about impugned decree on 16-10-2008. This case was filed on 20-10-2008. Since this case was filed within 30 (thirty) days from the date of knowledge of impugned decree, the case is not barred by limitation. The record and documents also so that the defendants petitioners were proforma defendants in the case and the suit properties appear to be government properties. Since the petitioners were not made principal defendants, there was made a situation that they did not contest the suit earlier. So it can be said that there were sufficient reasons behind their non-appearance in the suit. Accordingly points No. 2 and 3 are decided in favour of the petitioners. 

 5. Rule 13 Order IX speaks 'satisfaction' and this 'satisfaction' is satisfaction of the Court. From the facts of the case it appears that Government satisfactorily explained its non-appearance when the suit was decreed against Government. 

 7. On a reading of this law it appears that the aforesaid law before amendment government was impleaded as proforma defendant but after amendment, government became necessary party, as such, we find that learned Judge committed no illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Case and set-aside the ex-parte decree for fresh trial of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005. We find no substance in the rule.
